AUGUSTA, MAINE – Today September 4, marks just 60 days until the General Election on November 3. The Office of the Secretary of State today provided an update about Maine’s election processes for this stage of the election cycle.

Key dates to know:

  • September 15 - National Voter Registration Day
  • September 19 (45 days before Election Day) - Deadline to send UOCAVA ballots to already pending requests
  • October 4 (30 days before Election Day) - In-person, no-excuse absentee voting period begins (goes through close of business in a voter's town on Thurs., October 29)
  • October 20 - Election Hero Day
  • October 27 - Mock Election Day
  • October 29 - Last day to request a no-excuse absentee ballot
  • Registration deadlines:
    • In person: Close of the polls on Election Day.
    • Registering by mail or 3rd person: Received by the voter’s town or city by close of business 21 days before Election Day. (October 13) 
    • Registering online: 5 PM on the 21st day before Election Day. (October 13)
    • Registration through the BMV: On the 7th day before Election Day. (October 27)
    • UOCAVA voters in Title 21-A section 777-A by mail or electronically: By Noon the day before Election Day (November 2)
  • Absentee ballots:
    • Requesting an absentee ballot: Absentee ballots, including accessible ballots and ballots for uniformed and overseas voters, may be requested online at maine.gov/cgi-bin/online/AbsenteeBallot/index.pl. Voters may also contact their town hall to request a ballot or submit a paper application for an absentee ballot, and the request must be received at least three business days before Election Day (October 29), unless special circumstances exist.
    • Returning an absentee ballot: Only ballots received by 8 p.m. on Election Day are counted, regardless of postmark. In many towns and cities, voters have the option of returning an absentee ballot to a secured drop box. Maine voters can track the process of their ballot at: apps.web.maine.gov/cgi-bin/online/AbsenteeBallot/ballot_status.pl.

Absentee ballot processing

Absentee ballots may be processed up to seven days before Election Day, with notice provided to the Secretary of State and political parties 30 days before Election Day. A list of municipalities which may process ballots early will be available at maine.gov/sos/elections-voting/upcoming-elections at least one week prior to the start of early processing. Absentee ballot processing is a public process which may be observed by partisan and nonpartisan observers. Early processing may happen between the hours of 7 a.m. and 9 p.m., except when an inspection is requested. At such times, processing may not begin until the inspection period has concluded. Requests for inspection of absentee ballot applications and envelopes must be submitted in writing by 4 p.m. the day before each day of early processing. If such a request is made, the ballot applications and envelopes will be available an hour before early processing is set to begin.

During absentee ballot processing, teams of two work in stages. First, the absentee voter list is marked, then the ballots and envelopes separated, and only when a sufficient quantity of ballots has amassed, are the ballots unfolded and placed into the tabulator or ballot box. Ballots and envelopes are kept secure after each day of early processing. Absentee ballots are not counted until after 8 p.m. on Election Day, just as all other ballots. Many municipalities will conduct absentee ballot processing on Election Day itself, under the same procedures. 

Ranked-Choice Voting

With declared write-in candidates in both the U.S. Senate and the Congressional District 2 races, those races will be conducted by ranked choice. The ballots will include the names of the nominees as well as a blank write-in line with columns to rank candidate preferences. The list of declared write-in candidates is posted on the Secretary of State website and will be posted in polling locations. 

Ranked-choice voting, sometimes called "instant run-off voting," allows voters to choose their candidate(s) in order of preference, by marking candidates as their first, second and/or third choice. Voters may rank as many or as few candidates as they choose. 

In ranked-choice races, to win the race outright, a candidate must receive more than 50% of the first-choice votes as counted on Election Day. If no candidate receives 50% plus one vote of the total ballots cast in a particular race, then the tabulation will proceed to Augusta for the ranked-choice tabulation. The votes are tabulated in rounds, with the lowest-ranked candidates eliminated in each round until a remaining candidate receives a majority of the votes (more than 50%). The candidate who is determined to have received the majority of the votes (more than 50%) in the final round is declared the winner. MaineCare Comprehensive Benchmarking Report Initiation Notice

Aug 31, 2026

The Department initiated a comprehensive rate benchmarking report, as required by MRS Title 22 §3173-J. Rate reform law requires that, every four years, the Department compare MaineCare rates to the rates paid by the following:

  • Medicare
  • At least five comparison Medicaid states
  • Any appropriate Maine commercial payers

Interested parties will have the opportunity for public review and comment. The final report will be available on the MaineCare Rate System Reform webpage.

For questions please contact Megan Scott, MaineCare’s Legislative and Reform Coordinator.

*This notice is provided pursuant to Public Law 2022, Chapter 639.

WHEREAS
, the 130th Maine Legislature unanimously passed L.D. 1861, An Act to Establish the Safe Homes Program, and as Governor, I signed the bill into law on April 7, 2022; and
WHEREAS
, this bipartisan law promotes the safe storage of prescription drugs, firearms and other dangerous weapons in homes or public spaces; and
WHEREAS
, the Safe Homes Program is an optional, voluntary grant program that builds on the work of L.D. 1140, An Act To Establish a Sales Tax Exemption for the Purchase of Firearm Safety Devices, by making storage devices, such as gun safes, more affordable for people who want to buy them; and
WHEREAS
, the Safe Homes Program Fund will provide grants for purchasing safety devices for the safe storage of prescription drugs, firearms, and dangerous weapons in homes or public spaces; and
WHEREAS
, according to a report by the U.S. CDC, there were 181 deaths by firearms in the State of Maine in 2024, with over 86 percent of the deaths the result of suicide; and
WHEREAS
, in 2025, there were 390 confirmed and suspected fatal drug overdoses, 20.4 percent lower than the total confirmed fatal overdoses for 2024; and
WHEREAS
, by ensuring that firearms and prescription drugs are properly stored and secured, this law will reduce accidental gun deaths, prevent suicide, and improve public health; and
WHEREAS
, in accordance with 1 MRSA § 150-R, the month of September of each year is designated as Safe Homes Awareness Month to raise awareness of the importance of safety in the home and the assistance that is available through the Safe Homes Program established in Title 25, section 7001;
NOW, THEREFORE
, be it resolved that I, Janet T. Mills, Governor of the State of Maine, do hereby proclaim September 2026 as
Safe Homes Awareness Month
throughout the State of Maine, and I urge all citizens to recognize this observance, promote the proper storage of prescription drugs and firearms, and learn more about the assistance available through the Safe Homes Program.

Notice of Agency Rulemaking Proposal

 

AGENCY: Department of Health and Human Services, Office of MaineCare Services, Division of Policy

CHAPTER NUMBER AND RULE TITLE: 10-144 C.M.R. Ch. 101, MaineCare Benefits Manual (MBM), Ch. III, Sec. 20, Allowances for Home and Community-Based Services for Adults with Other Related Conditions

TYPE OF RULE: Major Substantive

BRIEF SUMMARY: Section 20 in the MBM authorizes home and community-based services (HCBS) under a CMS-approved Section 1915(c) waiver. The Department proposes to amend the Chapter III, Section 20 rule to establish the reimbursement methodology for new services being added under a companion, Chapter II, Section 20 rule, and to remove rates of reimbursement for all services which will now be listed in Rate Schedules on the Department’s website pursuant to 22 M.R.S. § 3177-J. The website address for current rates of reimbursement in the Department’s website and the statutory authority for this approach is stated in this proposed rule. Procedure codes, modifiers, and billable units remain in the rule, together with provisions for annual cost of living adjustments in conformance with 22 M.R.S. § 3173-J(2)(D)(3). Such cost-of-living adjustments will satisfy the requirements for direct support worker wages set forth in 22 M.R.S. § 7402(1).

See http://www.maine.gov/dhhs/oms/rules/index.shtml for rules and related rulemaking documents.

Once adopted, the proposed Chapter III, Section 20 rule will only be provisional: as a major substantive rule, Chapter III, Section 20 requires Legislative approval before it can be legally effective. Therefore, the Department anticipates also adopting an emergency Chapter III, Section 20 rule so that these methodology and rates changes will become legally effective on the same date as changes to the Chapter II, Section 20 routine technical rule becomes effective.

AGENCY: Department of Health and Human Services, MaineCare Services, Division of Policy

CHAPTER NUMBER AND RULE TITLE: 10-144 C.M.R. Ch. 101, MaineCare Benefits Manual (MBM) [Ch. I, Sec. 1, General Administrative Policies and Procedures]

TYPE OF RULE: Routine Technical

PROPOSAL FILING NUMBER: 2026-P195

BRIEF SUMMARY: This rulemaking is proposed via two, simultaneous private citizen petitions submitted to the Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) on June 23, 2026, to adopt or modify a rule. The petitioners provided the specific rule changes proposed here as part of their petitions. Under 5 M.R.S. § 8055, the Department of Health and Human Services (Department) is required to initiate rulemaking proceedings on the petitioners’ proposals within 60 days because each petition was signed by 150 or more registered voters. Because the Department may only propose one set of amendments to a rule at any given time, this rulemaking combines the two petitioned rule amendments into a single rulemaking.

The proposed rule would amend Chapter I, Section 1 of the MaineCare Benefits Manual (MBM) to require the Department to conduct in-person, On-Site Reviews and On-Site Inspections of MaineCare provider business or service locations and authorize the Department to impose sanctions when a provider fails to permit access to the Department for such On-Site Visit, Review, or Inspection. The proposed rule would require the Department to suspend a MaineCare provider’s claims payments, under defined criteria, and to escrow withheld payments upon notice of improper payment with the issuance of a Payment Suspension and Escrow Order (PSEO). The rule proposes to escrow such suspended and hold payments until a final determination is made as to the existence and amount of any improper payment. The petitioners also propose that the Department require providers under payment suspension to continue to deliver medically necessary covered services to current MaineCare members.

The petitioners also propose that the Department work with the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to obtain any necessary approvals to amend the State Plan to enact these reforms.

Important Information Regarding Cancellation of Certificate of Title:

Pursuant to Title 29-A, section §669, beginning on July 29, 2026, residents of the state of Maine are able to request cancellation of their Certificate of Title for Tiny Home or Manufactured Home for purposes of obtaining residential real property.


When a Tiny Home or Manufactured Home is permanently affixed to land that you own, or land where you have permission from the land owner via a signed sworn statement, you may request to cancel the Certificate of Title. Once the Certificate of Title is cancelled, the home becomes part of the residential real property instead of being treated as personal property. Under Maine law, this process is handled through the county Registry of Deeds and the Maine Secretary of State Bureau of Motor Vehicles.
 

How to Cancel your Certificate of Tittle for Tiny Home or Manufactured Home 

Before requesting cancellation of the title, make sure:

  • You own the Tiny Home or Manufactured Home and the land where it is located; and/or
  • The individual that owns the property has given a sworn signed statement of authorization.
  • The home has been permanently affixed to the property in accordance with Maine law.
  • Any existing liens have been released or the lienholder has agreed to release the lien upon cancellation of the title.

  • This process is not for double-wide mobile homes/trailers

1. Gather the required documentation

You will need to obtain the following documents before submitting your request:

  • The Original Certificate of Title
  • A description of the home, including;
    • Model Year
    • Manufacturer {make}
    • Width
    • Length
    • Identification Number/Serial Number
  • Lien Release Documentation, if applicable
  • The legal description of the real property
  • A sworn statement confirming:
    • You own both the land, and the Tiny Home or Manufactured Home, or a sworn statement from the property land owner
    • The home is permanently affixed to the property/ground

If you are unable to locate your current Certificate of Title for Tiny Home or Manufactured Home, you are able to request a duplicate title by printing off the Duplicate Title Request Application {MVT-8} and mailing it into our Bureau of Motor Vehicles office with a $33 check-or-moneyorder payable to "Secretary of State". Once a duplicate title is obtained, you wll then be able to continue to the next step.
2. Record the appropriate documents with the Registry of Deeds

Take all the above documents listed to the Registry of Deeds in the county where the property is located. The Registry of Deeds will record the documents as part of the public land records.

For further information on the nearest Registry of Deeds and other contact information, please Maine Registry of Deeds 

3. Submit the Request for Cancellation of Certificate of Title

After the documents above have been recorded, submit a completed MVT-61: Request for Cancellation of Certificate of Title for Tiny Home or Manufactured Housing and provide all original documentation that was recorded within the Registry of Deeds {photocopies are not accepted}. Be sure to include the Book and Page number from the prior step from the Registry of Deeds

4. Receive Confirmation and record Cancellation Letter with Registry of Deeds

Once the Secretary of State reviews and approves your request, you will be mailed a Cancellation Letter stating the process is complete. You must then have the Cancellation Letter document recorded within the county Registry of Deeds. This is a crucial step, as the application process is pending the verification of receipt and recording at the Registry of Deeds office.

5. Return proof of recording to the Bureau of Motor Vehicles

As mentioned above, this process is dependent on the documentation within the public record of the residential real property. Once that document has been recorded within the Registry of Deeds, please return proof of filing with the Bureau of Motor Vehicles via email, both of which are listed below;

Email: titles.bmv@maine.gov

Requirements may vary depending on the circumstances of the transaction. Property Definitions 

This section provides information to help homeowners, buyers, and other interested parties understand the types of construction, material, and installation that classify each type of home. By outlining these definitions. Read through the below definitions for the appropriate boxes to get more information.

Tiny Home Definition

Pursuant to Maine Statute 29-A, section §101, subsection 80-C, Maine's definition of a "Tiny Home" is a living space permanently constructed on a frame or chassis and designed for use as permanent living quarters that: 

  • Complies with American National Standards Institute standard A 119.5 on plumbing, propane, fire and life safety and construction or National Fire Protection Association standard 1192 on plumbing, propane and fire and life safety for recreational vehicles; 
  • Does not exceed 400 sq. feet in size; 
  • Does not exceed any dimension allowed for operation on a public way; 

  • Is a vehicle without motive power. 

Manufactured Home Definition

Pursuant to Maine Statute 29-A, section §101, subsection 32-B, Maine's definition of a "Manufactured Home" is a structural unit or units designed to be used as a dwelling or dwellings and constructed in a manufacturing facility and then transported by the use of its own chassis or placement on an independent chassis to a building site. 

"Manufactured housing" includes any type of building that is constructed at a manufacturing facility and then transported to a building site where it is used for housing and that may be purchased, sold, offered for sale or brokered by a licensee in the interim. Three types of manufactured housing are included: 

  • Units constructed after June 15, 1976; 
  • State-certified modular homes; 
  • Units constructed prior to June 15, 1976

How to Title your Tiny Home or Manufactured Home

A Certificate of Title establishes legal ownership of a Tiny Home or Manufactured Home in the State of Maine. The application process varies depending on whether the home is new or used and the year of the model. Beginning in 2009, The Bureau of Motor Vehicles began issuing titles for Manufactured Homes and in 2019, the Bureau of Motor Vehicles began issuing titles for Tiny Homes. 

Note: If the manufactured homeowner is deceased, additional documentation may be required depending on the circumstances. Please contact the Bureau of Motor Vehicles, before submitting your application.

1. Determine if the model year is eligible for a Certificate of Title

The following information regarding the home’s year and housing status will help determine which model years are eligible for a Certificate of Title.

  • Manufactured Home: The Secretary of State may issue a Certificate of Title for new or used manufactured housing that was previously issued a State of Maine Certificate of Title, or a model year 2007-or-later model that was never issued a Certificate of Title. 
     
  • Tiny Home: The Secretary of State shall issue certificates of title for new tiny homes beginning with model year 2020. The Secretary of State shall issue a Certificate of Title for a used tiny home of any model year that was previously issued a State of Maine Certificate of Title.
     
2. Identify who must apply for a Certificate of Title and what documents are required

There are generally four categories of individuals who may submit an application for a Certificate of Title. The submission process and required documentation may vary depending on whether the application is completed by the customer or the retail seller/dealer. Please refer to the document list below:

New home purchased from a Maine dealer: The retail seller submits the following:

  • MVT-60 Application, Certificate of Origin for a Manufactured Home or Tiny Home, Transfer of Ownership document, Required Fee of $100 payable via check or money order2

New home purchased outside Maine: The lienholder or owner submits the following:

  • MVT-60 Application, Certificate of Origin for a Manufactured Home or Tiny Home, Transfer of Ownership document, Required Fee of $100 payable via check or money order2
